verdict.rationale: cubic.yaml is described as living in the repo root as the 'source of truth' for review behavior and custom agents, which implies it can be versioned and reviewed like any other repo file via normal git workflows — but this is inferred from file location, not an explicit product feature for tracking, reviewing, or rolling back automation changes (e.g. no changelog, diff view, or revert UI for custom agents/policies is documented). missing for 10: explicit version-history or rollback UI for custom agents/rules, audit trail of automation changes, and any first-party or community evidence of reverting a prior automation configuration.
